title: Information, Unbiasedness, and Variance Certificates in Eligibility-Constrained Crossed Therapist Trials
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4.
gap_reasons: They do not characterize that intersection generally or resolve the advertised convex-eligibility sampler problem; the negative family is generated by replicating one eight-patient component, so no general design frontier is proved.

The variance repairs guarantee only expectation conservativeness under a prespecified outcome bound, with no variance consistency, one-batch coverage result, exact optimal inflation on the witness family, or evidence that the resulting intervals are practically useful.

proof_attempt_summary: Stage -0.5 accepted the revised field proposal, and one Stage 0 solve round discharged the theorem graph, leaving the convex-eligibility PSD-safe sampler decision explicitly open. The D0.5 math referee passed and verified the corrected Kennedy CLT citation, but the independent novelty referee graded the delivered result incremental and unsalvageable at the field floor because it did not characterize or construct PSD-safe lotteries generally. The fixed-policy PSD criterion, direct-sum obstruction family, variance corrections, and proof note remain usable for a genuinely stronger follow-on question.
tldr: In an eligibility-constrained crossed therapist trial, working-model information, design-unbiased estimation of a fixed therapist-policy effect, and conservative variance estimation require different certificates. Capacity parity determines the information optimum, every feasible policy \(W\) admits an attaining law with correct joint cells, and the ordinary contrast targets \(\tau_W\) exactly if and only if those cells equal \(w_{ij}/2\). The exact bounded zero-effect bias envelope is graph specific. Universal expected conservativeness is equivalent to a roster-slack PSD condition. An open interval of two-roster probabilities, replicated over any number of independent eligibility components, yields parity-optimal fixed-policy lotteries outside the PSD-safe subclass; the 72-state law with \(\operatorname{Var}(D)=3/32>1/16=\mathbb E\widehat U\) is the midpoint worked example. A bounded-outcome Gershgorin correction is conservative for every audited lottery, dominates the minimum-trace diagonal PSD inflation, is tight with it on the safe class, and is strictly larger on the midpoint direct-sum family. A two-mark dynamic program computes exact moments for a named bounded-treewidth Gibbs sampler in time polynomial only in the explicit patient-expanded, unary-capacity input for fixed width. Independent identical batches provide a standard inference repair, while PSD-safe sampler existence on binary-encoded convex eligibility inputs remains open.
gap: Existing crossed-trial, matching-lottery, and quadratic-variance results do not characterize the intersection of lotteries implementing a prespecified therapist policy with the roster-slack PSD-safe class, nor whether failure is stable under policy perturbation and disjoint replication.
fill: The project proves strict inclusion on an explicit open probability interval for every number of independent forced-roster components, preserves joint-cell unbiasedness and parity-optimal information throughout that family, supplies a complete-eligibility safe member, and proves that the Gershgorin correction dominates the minimum-trace diagonal correction with both equality and strict cases.
